thesis: Two commanders stand at opposite ends of one door — Brallin bills the table for every card that LEAVES your hand and Shabraz pays you for every card that ARRIVES — so the deck is a hand-refill machine whose output is entirely a function of who else is standing at those two doors when a wheel resolves.

stages.label: THIRTY-SIX LANDS, ONE BASIC, AND THE MONEY FOR THE SECOND WHEEL
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six lands, ONE of them a basic Island — this round's only change, in for Gleaming Bastion — plus Sol Ring, Arcane Signet and Treasure Map // Treasure Cove, plus three Treasure makers the wheel is supposed to pay for. The bill is two things on one turn: a 4- or 5-mana commander AND a 3-to-6-mana wheel on top, then {4} again every turn if the wheel is Queen Kayla. Measured (goldfish_metrics, 10,000 games, seed 42, model_version 4d9205d29b87): mean available mana 4.038 at T4, 5.535 at T6, 9.43 at T10; land-drop hit rate 0.825 at T4, 0.713 at T6. Blue is what binds — 54.1% of the pips on 32 land sources against a 36-source target, on-curve 0.785 ungated (mana_analysis), and 13 of 36 lands can enter tapped, 5 of them always. THE TYPED-LAND TRAP IS THE THING TO KNOW. Eight lands carry a basic land type — Glittering Massif, Hallowed Fountain, Irrigated Farmland, Island, Raugrin Triome, Sacred Foundry, Steam Vents, Thundering Falls — and five read a type off the board: Glacial Fortress and Sulfur Falls enter tapped without one; Floodfarm Verge and Riverpyre Verge make their first colour (W and R) unconditionally but gate their BLUE mode on 'a Plains or an Island' / 'an Island or a Mountain', and Nimbus Maze gates blue on 'a Plains', white on 'an Island', and makes only colourless with neither — so all three withhold blue until the right land is down. THE ISLAND SATISFIES A CLAUSE ON ALL FIVE: both Verges' blue, the Maze's WHITE, and the enters-untapped clause on Glacial Fortress and Sulfur Falls. The one it misses is the Maze's BLUE, which wants a Plains. It is the SIXTH Island-typed land here, not the first, so it adds an enabler rather than unlocking a gate. model_treasures is OFF by declaration, so the three Treasure makers add no mana above.

stages.label: THE TWELVE WHEELS YOU SPEND — AND THE SECOND KEY NOBODY DECLARES
stages.what_it_does: Nothing here starts itself: every payoff is a tax collector with nothing to tax until a hand empties and refills, which is why a wheel is the one group the declaration marks `required`. These twelve are the wheels you SPEND a card to fire; the five that wheel again and again are permanents and are filed as fuel. READ THE SPLIT INSIDE THIS STAGE BEFORE YOU CAST ONE. Six discard and therefore pay Brallin — Burning Inquiry, Khorvath's Fury, Reforge the Soul, Tolarian Winds, Windfall, and Magus of the Wheel, which sacrifices itself and needs a turn to untap first. Six shuffle or bottom and pay him nothing — Commit // Memory, Echo of Eons, Molten Psyche, Time Reversal, Whirlpool Warrior, Winds of Change — refilling you for the Shabraz half only, and refilling the table with you. Three refill only YOU: Tolarian Winds, Whirlpool Warrior's enters-trigger, and Khorvath's Fury if you call yourself friend. THE IGNITION IS A TWO-KEY DOOR AND ONLY ONE KEY IS DECLARED. The declaration's 17-card wheel group is drawn in 0.991 of games, 0.943 by turn six, mean turn 1.772; the 9-card DISCARD-wheel group 0.948 and 0.809, mean turn 2.946. A wheel is therefore never the thing you are waiting for. What you are waiting for is a payoff standing at the door: both partners on the battlefield is 0.834 by turn six, mean turn 5.395, never-both 0.011. That gap — 1.772 against 5.395 — is the ignition window, and no declared group measures it.

stages.label: THE WHEELS YOU DO NOT SPEND, AND THE CARDS BETWEEN THEM
stages.what_it_does: Five permanents wheel and keep wheeling: Anje's Ravager on every attack (it must attack), Queen Kayla for {4} and a tap once a turn at sorcery speed, Arjun on every spell you cast, Jace's Archivist for {U} and a tap, Teferi's Puzzle Box on every player's draw step. THREE OF THE FIVE REFILL ONLY YOU — Ravager, Kayla and Arjun — and that is the axis this deck is being bought on: branches/budget-v1/branch.json records two of them as the largest single-card gains measured on the list (+1.739 and +1.102 on damage@T8 against a stated MDE of 0.695, from an uncommitted slot sweep, not from the committed run). Arjun bottoms rather than discards, so he pays Shabraz and never Brallin. Around them sit the cards that keep the hand turning between wheels: Faithless Looting and Artist's Talent move one card at a time; Teferi's Ageless Insight doubles every draw but the first each draw step, so a seven-card refill is fourteen Shabraz triggers; Mind's Eye bills the opponents' half of a symmetric wheel at {1} a card, and the only other card in the 99 that reads an opponent DRAWING is Smothering Tithe, over in mana — Rhystic Study taxes their CASTS instead, which a wheel does not cause; Library of Leng puts what a wheel discards on top of your library instead of into the graveyard; Sorcerer Class loots two on arrival (four triggers between the pair) and at level 3 turns each instant or sorcery into damage to each opponent, and its level-2 mana reads ‘only to cast an instant or sorcery spell OR TO GAIN A CLASS LEVEL’ — so it cannot pay an ordinary activation (Kayla’s {4}, Jace’s {U}) but it DOES pay a Class level, which is an activated ability (716.2): its own {3}{U}{R}, and Artist’s Talent’s {2}{R} steps in this same stage.

stages.label: THE TOLLBOOTHS THAT PAY IN CARDS AND COUNTERS
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper on the value side: permanents that stand at the door and take something other than life. Shabraz is the whole draw half — a +1/+1 counter and a life for every card that arrives — and the pair's counters measure 6.78 by T6 and 38.457 by T10 (their own counters only). CADENCE is what to read here, not the count. Rielle fires ONCE on the first discard each turn and draws that many, so a seven-card wheel draws seven more and pays every per-draw tollbooth twice. Ivora takes a counter per discarded card and makes Blood on arrival. Containment Construct lets you replay a discarded card that turn; Currency Converter exiles discards and buys them back later as a Treasure or a 2/2. Curator of Mysteries pays scry 1, which is selection and not advantage. Chasm Skulker grows one counter per draw and is in the declared AIR KILL component despite having no evasion — its death tokens have islandwalk, not flying. Mindless Automaton and Jaxis are the opposite shape: you PAY mana and discard one card at a time, so they do not scale with a wheel at all. Marketback Walker turns its counters into cards only when it dies. Priced from the brief: the 6-card 'discard converted to board or cards' component is drawn in 0.936 of games, 0.714 by turn six, mean turn 3.824.

evidence.note: the seven Shabraz triggers and the seven Brallin triggers are one batch off one resolution

stages.label: THE TOLLBOOTHS THAT PAY IN LIFE TOTALS
stages.what_it_does: Brallin is the discard half and the deck's declared clock: 1 damage to EACH opponent per card discarded, plus a counter, so a seven-card wheel is 7 to three seats — PROVED by stack 001. The second per-discard source is a two-card component (Glint-Horn Buccaneer, Magmakin Artillerist) drawn in 0.66 of games and 0.343 by turn six — with commander protection at 0.342 it is the thinnest PAIR of the twelve declared groups, a tie and not a rank (notes[12]). The two are not the same card: Glint-Horn bills PER CARD (seven triggers off a seven-card wheel) and Magmakin bills PER EVENT ('whenever you discard one or more cards, that much damage'), one trigger of seven. Identical totals until Artist's Talent is at level 3, and stack 004 PROVES the difference: its +2 is a replacement on each noncombat damage EVENT, once per event. On the draw half, Psychosis Crawler and Niv-Mizzet bill every card that arrives, while Irencrag Pyromancer bills the SECOND draw each turn, which is once a turn and not once a card. READ THE FIGURE WITH ITS DEFINITION: cumulative event damage against ONE seat is 6.769 at T8 and 15.703 at T10, and that is the whole ping pillar — it does not close a 40-life seat on its own. It IS inside the kill rate: goldfish_turn.py 1899-1904 takes event damage off the same opponent_life the combat step reads and can set kill_turn, so the pings are the minor share — 6.769 cumulative by T8 against 81.741 of combat over the same eight turns (mean_damage_by_turn summed 1-8, the like-for-like figure), 7.6% against 92.4%. Three ignition cards carry their own rider — Khorvath's Fury, Molten Psyche's metalcraft, Sorcerer Class level 3.

evidence.note: seven discards, seven Brallin triggers, 7 to each seat
Artist's Talent at level 3 taxes each damage EVENT, which splits Glint-Horn from Magmakin

stages.label: SIX WAYS TO KEEP A 3/3 ON THE TABLE, AND WHAT V4 ACTUALLY BOUGHT
stages.what_it_does: The engine is two 3/3s costing {3}{R} and {3}{W}{U}, and every figure on this page assumes they are alive. V4's one swap lands here: Astral Drift OUT, Shelter IN. ENUMERATE THE SIX BEFORE READING THE SUPERLATIVE. Lightning Greaves (shroud) and Swiftfoot Boots (hexproof) protect only once attached and EQUIP IS SORCERY SPEED — a two-card declared component drawn in 0.661 of games and 0.342 by turn six — with the second per-discard source at 0.343 the thinnest PAIR of the twelve declared groups, a tie and not a rank (notes[12]). Nezahal protects only Nezahal, at three discards (three more Brallin triggers paid to dodge a removal spell). Nimble Obstructionist has flash but counters an ACTIVATED OR TRIGGERED ABILITY only — it cannot answer a Swords to Plowshares. Decree of Silence cycles at instant speed for {4}{U}{U} and counters target spell, so it IS instant-speed protection — at six mana. Shelter is therefore not the only instant-speed answer; it is the only card in the 99 that protects a creature at instant speed by TARGETING IT, for {1}{W}, and the only one that draws a card while doing it — which is itself a Shabraz trigger and a Niv-Mizzet or Psychosis Crawler ping. Know its edges: protection from a colour stops damage, enchanting, equipping, blocking and targeting, so it beats Swords, a targeted burn spell and a chump block, and it does NOT beat an untargeted wrath. Talon Gates of Madara also targets a creature and phases it out, but it does so on a LAND PLAY, which is sorcery speed and once. Astral Drift was gated on CYCLING, not discarding, so it never paid Brallin. Interaction is mana-starved rather than card-starved: in hand in 0.521 of games at T6, castable in 0.069.

stages.label: THE AIR FORCE THE DRAWS BUILD
stages.what_it_does: The declaration names two kills off one ignition, and this is the DOMINANT pillar of the measured kill, not the whole of it: kill_by_turn reads ONE 40-life total that both pillars lower — goldfish_turn.py subtracts event damage from opponent_life and lets it set kill_turn (1899-1904) before the combat step does the same (2133-2136) — so the rates below are combat plus pings. The share only means anything if BOTH halves are cumulative: combat summed over turns 1-8 (mean_damage_by_turn) is 81.741 against 6.769 of cumulative ping damage — 92.4% against 7.6%, which is what makes this the air force's figure. Every card that arrives is a 1/1 flier with haste (The Locust God) or a 1/1 Faerie on the second draw each turn (Improbable Alliance) or a foreshadow counter toward an 8/8 Kraken (Ominous Seas); every card that leaves is a 2/2 Drake for {1} (Drake Haven, on a discard OR a cycle); Shark Typhoon cycles for an X/X flier at instant speed; Vanguard Suppressor squads and draws on connect. Kefnet is indestructible and cannot attack unless you hold seven cards, which is exactly the hand a wheel leaves. Silent Hallcreeper cannot be blocked. Stromkirk Noble, Waterbender Ascension and Gossip's Talent are connect-and-grow support, and two of the three are in the model's own blind-spot list (combat_effects_not_modelled: Generous Plunderer, Gossip's Talent, Stromkirk Noble). Enduring Curiosity turns each connection back into a card, which pays Shabraz again. Measured: THE AIR KILL assembles in 0.848 of games, 0.540 by turn six, mean turn 4.987; board power 9.807 at T6 and 19.011 at T10; bodies 2.410 and 7.517; kill rate against one unopposed 40-life seat 0.207 by T6, 0.631 by T7, 0.888 by T8, mean kill turn 7.245.

map_disagreements.why: Six cards do ONE job — bill a life total per card that moves — and the map files them by what else they say. Glint-Horn, Magmakin and Irencrag read as red creatures and sit in Bodies (city-0); Niv-Mizzet and Psychosis Crawler read as draw engines and sit in Finishers (city-2); Brallin reads as a counters payoff and sits in Payoffs (city-3). The one function this deck is built on has three addresses because no card in the set says 'per discard' and 'per draw' in the same sentence.

map_disagreements.component: THE WHEELS YOU DO NOT SPEND (the fuel stage)
map_disagreements.why: Twelve cards across four cities. The split is one-shot-versus-permanent, which is a property of the TYPE LINE and not of the text: Faithless Looting and Teferi's Puzzle Box land in Card Flow beside the sorcery wheels, Anje's Ravager and Queen Kayla in Bodies beside creatures that do nothing alike, Rhystic Study and Mind's Eye in Finishers, Sorcerer Class in Ramp on its level-2 mana. A repeatable wheel and a one-shot wheel read identically to a text embedding and behave completely differently at the table.

Brallin and Shabraz sit in the SAME city (city-3), which is the map agreeing — and it agrees for the wrong reason. They cluster on '+1/+1 counter' with Chasm Skulker, Ivora, Marketback Walker, Silent Hallcreeper and Stromkirk Noble, i.e. on the half of each commander's text that matters least. The damage clause and the life clause, which are the whole deck, are invisible to the clustering.
